host.description: A 1024x1024 pixel-art canvas that a person and an AI agent edit together, live, on the same page, through WebMCP site tools.

entries.description: Six in-page WebMCP tools for drawing, reading back, rearranging, undoing, framing and exporting pixel art on a shared 1024x1024 canvas. Registered by the page itself; there is no remote MCP endpoint.
representativeQueries: draw a sprite on a shared pixel canvas
edit pixel art together with a person in the browser
what WebMCP tools does this page expose
make a 32x32 pixel mushroom and export it as a PNG

entries.description: How to use the six MCPixels tools well — the rows-and-palette wire format, ops strings, mirroring, reading before redrawing, and the token budget behind those choices.
representativeQueries: how do I draw pixel art with the MCPixels tools
what is the rows and palette format for draw_pixel_art
how do I move or duplicate art already on the canvas
how do I read the canvas back before editing it

entries.description: Short orientation for agents arriving at mcpixels.app: what the site is, what the tools do, and where the rest of the discovery documents live.
representativeQueries: how do agents use this site
where is the documentation for this pixel editor

entries.description: States that MCPixels needs no credentials, no registration and no tokens: the canvas is local to the browser tab and the tools run in the page.
representativeQueries: how does an agent authenticate with mcpixels
does mcpixels need an API key
is there an agent registration endpoint for mcpixels
